steps.say: Every sound is made by something vibrating. Vibrating means moving quickly back and forth.

figure.alt: A drum, a guitar and a bell.

steps.say: Touch your throat while you hum. You can feel your voice box vibrating.
Vibrations travel through materials to your ear. Sound travels through solids, liquids and gases.
Sound cannot travel through empty space. There is nothing there to vibrate.
Sound gets fainter as it travels further from where it was made.
Inside your ear, the vibrations make your eardrum vibrate. Your brain hears this as sound.

check.prompt: What makes the sound when you pluck a guitar string?

options.why: Strings do not give out light.
Something must move to make a sound.

hints: All sounds are made by this kind of movement.
check.explanation: The plucked string vibrates. The vibrations travel through the air to your ears.

check.prompt: Sound cannot travel through empty space because there is no ___ to carry it.
hints: On Earth, sound travels through something all around us.
check.explanation: Sound needs a material, like air, to travel through. Empty space has no air.
